positions.name: GateAuthorityFromIncident
positions.frame: how does citing a past incident function to justify imposing a new deployment precondition?
positions.why: src-1 performs the directive as a settled rule ('now requires'), and src-2 grounds that rule in a concrete prior failure ('two unsigned artifacts reach staging... that is the whole reason for the gate'). Read together, the incident recall is doing legitimating work for the authority move — the ranking gesture in src-1 is backed by the rational-persuasion appeal in src-2, per the relational and power reads. No tension: both expressions point the same direction, from incident toward mandate.

positions.name: GateFormalParameters
positions.frame: how is the gate rule restated as a set of fixed operational parameters (rule, scope, owner)?
positions.why: src-3, src-4, and src-5 share the bolded-label-colon-compressed-clause cadence (style mint-1) and each performs a settled, declarative parameter of the same gate — the rule itself, its environmental scope, and its named accountable owner — all read as conservation-value, legitimate-authority, decision-conviction restatements rather than arguments. They cohere as one directional read: the gate decomposed into its fixed operational fields.
